title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
notes: A pair of linear equations a1x+b1y+c1=0 and a2x+b2y+c2=0 can be solved graphically or algebraically (substitution, elimination).
Graphically, two lines can: intersect at one point (unique solution -- consistent), be coincident (infinite solutions -- dependent & consistent), or be parallel (no solution -- inconsistent).
Ratio test: a1/a2 != b1/b2 -> intersecting (unique solution). a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 -> coincident (infinite solutions). a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 -> parallel (no solution).
Substitution method: express one variable in terms of the other from one equation, plug into the second equation, solve.
Elimination method: multiply equations to make coefficients of one variable equal, then add/subtract to eliminate it.
If, during elimination/substitution, the variable cancels out and you get a TRUE statement (like 18=18) -> infinitely many solutions. If you get a FALSE statement (like -4=0) -> no solution.
Word problems are the heart of this chapter: ages, numbers/digits, fractions, cost problems, speed/distance -- always define variables clearly first, form two equations, then solve.

formulas.name: Consistency test
formulas.use: Determine unique / infinite / no solution without graphing.

formulas.name: Two-digit number
formulas.formula: Number = 10x + y (x=tens digit, y=units digit); reversed = 10y + x

formulas.name: Substitution method
formulas.formula: Solve one eqn for a variable, substitute into the other
formulas.use: Best when one equation is already simple to isolate a variable.

formulas.name: Elimination method
formulas.formula: Scale equations so one variable's coefficients match, then add/subtract

examples.question: Check graphically whether x+3y=6 and 2x-3y=12 is consistent; solve if so.
examples.solution: Plotting both lines, they intersect at (6,0). So the pair is consistent with unique solution x=6, y=0.

examples.question: Ratio of incomes of two persons is 9:7, ratio of expenditures is 4:3. Both save Rs 2000/month. Find incomes.
examples.solution: Let incomes=9x,7x; expenditures=4y,3y. 9x-4y=2000, 7x-3y=2000. Scale to eliminate y: multiply eqn1 by3, eqn2 by4 -> 27x-12y=6000, 28x-12y=8000. Subtract: x=2000. Sub back: y=4000. Incomes = 18000 and 14000.

examples.question: Sum of a two-digit number and its digit-reversal is 66; digits differ by 2. Find the number(s).
examples.solution: x+y=6 (from sum condition /11) and x-y=2 or y-x=2. Solving both cases gives numbers 42 and 24 -- two valid answers.

exercises.question: (i) 10 students took a quiz, girls are 4 more than boys -- find boys & girls graphically. (ii) 5 pencils+7 pens cost Rs50, 7 pencils+5 pens cost Rs46 -- find cost of each.
Classify consistent/inconsistent, solve graphically if consistent: (i) x+y=5, 2x+2y=10 (ii) x-y=8, 3x-3y=16 (iii) 2x+y-6=0, 4x-2y-4=0 (iv) 2x-2y-2=0, 4x-4y-5=0
exercises.answer: (i) Consistent, infinite solns, y=5-x (ii) Inconsistent (iii) Consistent, unique soln x=2,y=2 (iv) Inconsistent

exercises.topic: Forming Equations for Given Line Type
exercises.question: Given 2x+3y-8=0, write another equation so the pair is: (i) intersecting (ii) parallel (iii) coincident.
exercises.answer: Any one valid example each, e.g. (i) 3x+2y-7=0 (ii) 2x+3y-12=0 (iii) 4x+6y-16=0

exercises.question: Draw graphs of x-y+1=0 and 3x+2y-12=0. Find vertices of the triangle formed with the x-axis.
Solve by substitution: (i) x+y=14, x-y=4 (ii) s-t=3, s/3+t/2=6 (iii) 3x-y=3, 9x-3y=9 (iv) 0.2x+0.3y=1.3, 0.4x+0.5y=2.3 (v) root2 x+root3 y=0, root3 x-root8 y=0 (vi) (3x/2)-(5y/3)=-2, x/3+y/2=13/6
exercises.answer: (i) x=9,y=5 (ii) s=9,t=6 (iii) infinite solutions y=3x-3 (iv) x=2,y=3 (v) x=0,y=0 (vi) x=2,y=3

exercises.question: 5 years hence Jacob's age = 3x his son's; 5 years ago Jacob's age = 7x his son's. Find present ages.
Solve by elimination and substitution: (i) x+y=5, 2x-3y=4 (ii) 3x+4y=10, 2x-2y=2 (iii) 3x-5y-4=0, 9x=2y+7 (iv) x/2+2y/3=-1, x-y/3=3

(i) Fraction reduces to 1 if 1 added to numerator & 1 subtracted from denominator; becomes 1/2 if 1 added to denominator only. (ii) 5 yrs ago Nuri was thrice Sonu's age; 10 yrs later Nuri will be twice Sonu's age. (iii) Sum of digits of 2-digit no. is 9; 9x the number = 2x its reverse. (iv) Meena withdrew Rs2000 in Rs50 & Rs100 notes only, got 25 notes total. (v) Library: fixed charge for first 3 days + extra per day; Rs27 for 7 days, Rs21 for 5 days.
